papers.sections_read: All of v1 and v2 via arXiv HTML: Abstract; Introduction; Background (Time Series Forecasting; Models for time series data; Autoregressive Forecasting and MPI); FlowState (SSM Encoder Eq.1-2 + ZOH formulas; Functional Basis Decoder Eq.3-5; Adjusting Delta Eq.6; Parallel forecasts Eq.7; Causal normalization Eq.8-10); Experiments (Evaluation Setup, Metrics, Temporal Scaling, Context and Forecasting Length); Results Tables 1-3; Robustness to Unseen Sampling Rates (Fig.3); Ablation Table 4; Conclusion.
papers.mechanism: Encoder: a stack of N S5 layers. Each is a ZOH-discretized complex diagonal MIMO SSM (HiPPO init) followed by an MLP, with a skip connection. There is no patching. Decoder (FBD): the final encoder output at the last context step is read as coefficients of a Legendre basis. The resulting continuous function is sampled at spacing Delta. A single scale factor s_Delta multiplies Delta (Eq.6), which rediscretizes the SSM and rescales the decoder sampling. Training uses causal RevIN (running mean/std) and parallel forecasts from every prefix.
papers.input_reconstruction: Implicit ZOH only. The S5 ZOH formulas are applied to the raw samples on a uniform grid. There is no linear/spline reconstruction and no explicit continuous input path.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every observation (every sample index): the MLP after each S5 block, the residual/normalization, and causal RevIN (a per-step division by the running std). Background states that only the SSM output carries the nonlinearity.
papers.time_handling: Uniform grid. dt enters only as Delta*s_Delta (step-size rescaling) in the ZOH discretization and in the FBD output spacing. s_Delta is chosen from seasonality (s = 24/seasonality), not from the raw frequency. Effective context and horizon are L/s and T/s. No timestamps, no irregular dt.
papers.invariance_claim: Informal and empirical. The title says 'Sampling Rate Invariant'. The text says rescaling Delta gives 'similar representations, irrespective of the sampling rate'. There is no formal definition and no proof in v1/v2.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Real downsampling only. Loop Seattle, originally 5-min, is subsampled to 5..65 min in 5-min steps, target length 480, compared against TiRex, Chronos-bolt-b and Toto. The subsampling method (decimation or averaging) is not specified. Ablation 'w/o time-scale adjustment'. No knot refinement, no interpolation/upsampling, no missing-vs-rate separation, no irregular sampling.

papers.mechanism: Encoder: 6 layers. Each is an S5-like complex diagonal SSM with an output gate, h_t = c_t*sigmoid(W c_t + b) + D x_t (Eq.3), followed by an MLP and norm/residual. It is ZOH-discretized with a trainable per-state Delta_E in R^P. FBD: Legendre basis coefficients taken from the last encoder output and sampled at spacing Delta_F. There are separate scale factors s_E (encoder) and s_F (decoder), Eq.7. Setting s_E != s_F gives forecasts at a different rate than the input, e.g. an ETTh1 context producing an ETTm1-rate forecast.
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH, stated explicitly (Eq.19: u~(t)=u(floor(t/Delta)Delta)). The linear SSM is solved exactly for this piecewise-constant reconstruction. The paper says the only approximation comes from the ZOH reconstruction. No linear-interpolation/FOH reconstruction.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every observation index: the output gate (sigmoid), the MLP, the residual and normalization, and causal RevIN. B.1 calls these 'pointwise operations ... act independently at each time step' and argues they add no temporal discretization error, only a Lipschitz amplification.
papers.time_handling: Step-size rescaling only: Delta_E -> s_E*Delta_E (all P per-state Deltas scaled by one scalar), and decoder spacing -> s_F*Delta. The grid is uniform with fixed dt per sequence. A selective (input-dependent) Delta_E was tried and hurt performance. The scale factor is set from seasonality (Algorithm 1) or from automatic seasonality detection (D.2.2). Decoder 'time noise' jitters the sampling locations during training.
papers.invariance_claim: Approximate sampling-rate equivariance. Eq.8: F_{Delta'}(x) ~ FBD_{Delta'}(SSM_Delta(x)). Prop B.3 bounds the gap between final states under two ZOH reconstructions of the same Lipschitz-M input by (||B||M/alpha)(1-e^{-alpha T}) max{Delta,Delta'}. Single-layer end-to-end: error <= C max{Delta,Delta'} (Eq.46-47). Multi-layer: only a recursion E_l <= L_l E_{l-1} + C_l max{Delta,Delta'} is sketched, under assumed Lipschitz inputs to each layer. The paper never claims exact invariance, and knot refinement is not a special case it discusses. Its bound gives a nonzero first-order error for a piecewise-linear path with slope M.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Real downsampling only. ETT1m (15-min) resampled to 15..135 min in 15-min steps, H=480, vs TiRex, TimesFM-2.5 and Chronos-2-Synth (Fig.4); the resampling method is not specified. ETTh1 context used to forecast at ETTm1 rate (Fig.2). Cosine-similarity maps of last-layer encodings, ETT1m (s=0.25) vs ETT1h (s=1), temporally aligned vs time-flipped (B.2 Fig.8). Scale-factor sweep on ETTm1 (D.2.3). Not tested: virtual-knot insertion, interpolation upsampling, random drop, irregular grids. Missing data: the pretraining series with many NaNs are split into shorter series (C.2). No knot-vs-measurement distinction.

Sec 4: "sampling the continuous input x at a different rate yields (approximately) the same latent state and thus the same continuous forecast, which can then be evaluated on any grid."

papers.notes: This is the closest prior work to N2 and must be cited. (i) It already defines sampling-rate equivariance of a continuous-time forecast and proves a first-order ZOH mismatch bound. Prop B.3 is a standard ZOH/variation-of-constants inequality and should be marked as existing. (ii) It explicitly argues that per-sample pointwise ops add no discretization error. This is exactly the claim N2's counterexample targets: in layers l>1 the SSM integrates a ZOH hold of a per-sample nonlinear sequence, so the gap is O(Delta), not zero. (iii) Its FBD already provides continuous-time output querying: forecasts can be sampled at any spacing via s_F. N2's output query rule must credit this. (iv) It has no FOH/exact-path integration, no fixed physical-time clock for the nonlinearities, no exactness claim, and no knot-vs-measurement distinction. Author name: IBM and NeurIPS pages list 'Thomas Bohnstingl' where arXiv lists 'Thomas Ortner'. Papers citing FlowState that I checked (TinyCast 2608.15767, Forecast Collapse 2608.14106, EXAONE Finance 2609.04239, Toto 2.0 2605.20119; abstracts only) do not address sampling-grid invariance.

papers.mechanism: FlowStateModel.forward: (1) with_missing: NaN -> 0 plus a mask channel, so the input is [value, mask]; for MPI, mask_n all-masked steps are appended. (2) Causal RevIN: running mean/std over observed counts (cumsum), a per-step normalization. (3) Linear embedding 2->512. (4) Encoder, 6x FlowStateS5Layer: skip; S5Block (ZOH kernel, FFT convolution over the whole sequence, Re(C x), optional output gate sigmoid(Wy)*y, +D*u); MLP ('transformer' in r1.1: RMSNorm -> w3(silu(w1 x)*w2 x) + skip; 'gated' in v1.0: selu then x*sigmoid(Wx)); LayerNorm; residual. The last layer returns only positions from min_context-1 on. (5) FBD: Linear(512 -> 256 basis x 9 quantiles). Legendre basis of degree 255 (decoder_type 'legs'), evaluated at t_k = -1 + k*s*1.95/decoder_patch_len for k=1..int(decoder_patch_len/s) on the range [-1, 0.95], divided by 4. (6) De-normalize with the last-step RevIN statistics. FlowStateForPrediction stitches MPI patches, recomputes the quantiles, and returns the mean or median.
papers.input_reconstruction: None beyond an implicit ZOH. The kernel is exp(s*lambda*Delta*k) on a uniform index grid, with B_bar = (exp(s*lambda*Delta)-1)/lambda * B (exact ZOH). The time axis is the sample index only, with no timestamps.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Per sample, in every layer: causal RevIN division (once, at input), output gate sigmoid (r1.1), SwiGLU with RMSNorm or selu*sigmoid (v1.0), and LayerNorm. All act on every time index of the input grid.
papers.time_handling: scale_factor s is a scalar per batch element. In the encoder it multiplies exp(log_Delta) (P=512 per-state Deltas per layer, initialised log-uniform in [1e-3, 1e-1]). lambda = -exp(log_Lambda_real) + i*Lambda_imag, B, C and D are unchanged. In the decoder it multiplies the basis sampling spacing and sets the patch length int(decoder_patch_len/s). In FlowStateForPrediction it sets the context truncation max_context = min(16384, int(context_length/s)) - mask_n. The FFT convolution needs a uniform grid, so there is no per-step dt and irregular sampling cannot be represented. Missing values are masked tokens on the same grid. get_fixed_factor maps a pandas freq string plus domain to s = 24/seasonality.
papers.invariance_claim: The code makes none. Docstrings describe scale_factor as adjusting 'Delta of the S5 block and the Functional Basis Decoder'. The model card says it moves to a 'timescale invariant coefficient space'.
papers.grid_changes_tested: The official notebook demonstrates decimation only: context[:, ::4] with scale_factor 24/6. No tests of interpolation or knot insertion.

For a knot-refinement test with factor r: pass the refined series with scale_factor=s/r and prediction_length=H*r, and compare refined forecast indices r-1::r with the original. angle_summary:
FlowState (ICML 2026 as arXiv v3; a NeurIPS 2025 workshop version is OpenReview R50AT6nAsM) is the closest prior work in this angle, but it does not contain N2's central claim.

What FlowState does:
- **Encoder:** 6 S5-like complex diagonal SSM layers, ZOH-discretized with trainable per-state Delta_E. One scalar scale factor s multiplies all Deltas; A, B, C and D are unchanged.
- **Per-sample nonlinearities:** at every sample index there is causal RevIN, an output gate sigmoid(Wc)*c (r1.1), an MLP (SwiGLU+RMSNorm in r1.1, selu+sigmoid gate in v1.0), LayerNorm and a residual.
- **Decoder (FBD):** a Legendre ('legs') basis of degree 255 on [-1, 0.95], evaluated at spacing s*1.95/patch_len.
- **Grid and missing data:** the code uses an FFT convolution on a uniform grid. There are no timestamps and no per-step dt. Missing values become NaN masked tokens on the same grid (the TiRex style).
- **Formal claim (v3):** only approximate equivariance. Prop B.3 is a standard two-rate ZOH/variation-of-constants bound, O(M max{Delta, Delta'}). The multi-layer case is only sketched. The paper explicitly states that per-step pointwise ops 'do not introduce additional temporal discretization error'. That statement is exactly what N2's counterexample should target.
- **Experiments:** they test only real downsampling. Loop Seattle 5-65 min (v1/v2), ETTm1 15-135 min, ETTh1 context forecast at ETTm1 rate, encoder-correlation maps, and the notebook's [::4] decimation. They never test virtual-knot insertion, interpolation, random drop or irregular grids, and never distinguish knots from measurements.

Overlap with N2's four components:
- **Exact input integration:** partial. Exact ZOH solves the linear SSM exactly, but for a piecewise-constant reconstruction, not FOH.
- **Fixed-time nonlinearity:** none.
- **Refinement-invariance claim:** partial (approximate and first-order only).
- **Knot-vs-measurement distinction:** none.

What N2 must credit as existing:
- the notion of sampling-rate equivariance of a continuous-time forecast;
- dt-only rescaling (S4, S5, FlowState);
- ZOH mismatch bounds (FlowState Prop B.3);
- continuous-time output querying through a basis decoder (FBD, which also allows s_E != s_F);
- exact dilation equivariance of the continuous HiPPO-LegS operator (Prop 3), which is about dilation, not refinement.

S5, S4 and HiPPO all apply nonlinearities per step and test only decimation or timestamp scaling. Calibration numbers:
- Speech Commands 35-class, 16k to 0-shot 8k: S5 96.52 to 94.53.
- SC10 at 0.5x frequency: S4 98.32 to 96.30.
- Character Trajectories 100 to 200 Hz: HiPPO-LegS 88.8.
- None of these papers reports HAR, EigenWorms or PDM.

My own CPU check of FlowState r1.1 (not a paper result): refining a synthetic series by r=2 on its piecewise-linear interpolant, with s/2, left the forecast about 2-3% different at common times. The last-layer representation changed much more (cosine 0.908). The layer-wise difference grows with depth, from 0.8% after causal RevIN to 4-9% at layer 0 and roughly 40% at layers 3-4. This is a concrete counterexample on a real pretrained model, consistent with N2's hypothesis.

Its coefficient vector x[n] is then decimated to a FIXED output rate by keeping one vector every K_PDM = K_PCM x OSR samples (no anti-alias filter). All nonlinear processing (an S4D-style SSM stack with dense layers for KWS; LiSenNet for speech enhancement) runs only on this fixed-rate decimated sequence. For SE the predicted coefficients are projected back onto the basis at the PCM rate and overlap-added.

Decimating below Nyquist 'without anti-aliasing' is justified by the overlapping memory windows and the low-pass spectra of the LegT/FouT bases, not by any guarantee.

angle_summary:
(1) Main finding. Boulanger & Wood, arXiv 2608.28472 (Aug 2026), already publishes the core N2 architecture. A fixed LegT/FouT continuous-time SSM runs at the input rate with bilinear Δ = 1/f_s. Its state is decimated to a fixed physical rate (hop K_PDM = K_PCM×OSR, "without anti-aliasing"), and every nonlinear layer (an S4D KWS stack, LiSenNet SE) runs only on that fixed-rate sequence. The paper claims a "modulation- and sampling-rate-invariant" latent. N2 therefore cannot claim "linear stem + nonlinearities on a fixed physical clock" or "multirate SSM front end" as new. Overlap is substantial on the fixed-clock component and none on exact integration.

What that paper does not do:
- It is not exact: bilinear discretization on raw samples, no piecewise-linear/FOH reconstruction.
- It proves nothing. The invariance is empirical and approximate ("nearly identical up to quantization noise").
- Grids are integer-OSR and aligned. There are no non-integer ratios, irregular timing or missing data, and no clock points between observations.
- PCM→PDM changes the signal (cubic spline + ΣΔ), so it is not a lossless knot refinement.
- It does not separate knot refinement, real downsampling and missing data.

For PDM, this architecture is a mandatory baseline. If N2's gain disappears against it or against fixed-grid resampling, the verdict is NO_GO.

(2) Rough Transformer (arXiv 2405.20799) is the closest non-SSM precedent. It linearly interpolates the samples, computes exact closed-form signatures at "a fixed set of time points" independent of sample count, and runs nonlinearities (attention, MLP) only there. Its Prop. 3.1 claims only T(X)≈T(X′), and the tests are random drops. Signatures of a piecewise-linear path are unchanged by inserting collinear knots, so exact stem invariance to virtual knots is a known property there, although the paper never states it. It must be a near-work baseline (resampling/fixed-grid + Transformer family). Log-NCDE/NRDE also separate an exact log-signature path summary from the nonlinear vector field, but their intervals are index-based (e.g. 4 observations) and the nonlinear part runs inside an ODE solver.

(3) Existing results N2 must label as prior work:
- Exact FOH closed-form discretization in deep SSMs: FSSM 2509.08458 (Eq. 4 derivation); the Vision Mamba discretization study 2604.20606 (FOH Eq. 6).
- Mamba-3 (2603.15569) uses an approximate exponential-trapezoidal rule.
- The ODE/ZOH mismatch bound ‖s^Δ−s^Δ′‖ ≤ (‖B‖M/α)(1−e^{−αT})·max{Δ,Δ′} and its multi-layer O(max Δ) recursion: FlowState 2508.05287 v3, App. B.1, Prop. B.3, Eqs 49-54.
- FlowState keeps a per-step MLP after every S5 layer and asserts pointwise operations "do not introduce additional temporal discretization error". Per-step outputs are re-held (ZOH) as the next layer's input, so this is the natural target for N2's per-observation-nonlinearity counterexample. FlowState bounds the effect at O(Δ) and never claims zero.

(4) Other multirate/multiscale SSMs have no physical-time invariance:
- Index-based: SaShiMi (reshape pooling), MS-SSM 2512.23824 (dilated SWT-style conv plus per-scale SSMs), HiSS (fixed 50 Hz resampling + chunking, the mandatory resampling+SSM baseline family), EventSSM (exact impulse-input update but event-count pooling before nonlinearities).
- dt-only: ms-Mamba (Δ as an internal multi-scale knob, explicitly "not an input downsampling"), the event-camera SSMs of Zubić et al. (Δ rescaling plus band-limiting; mAP 47.71→39.84 from 20 to 200 Hz), TIDES 2605.09742 (physical Δ, but token-wise selectivity and nonlinearity).
- S-Edge (Machine Learning 2025): per-layer naive decimation with Ts rescaling and RZOH augmentation. Nonlinearities stay on grids tied to the input.
- 2410.08681: "irregular" means variable observation-set size; its "resampling" is cross-attention.
- VISTA-SSM: a linear-Gaussian clustering model with Euler Δ.
None of these makes an exact refinement claim or separates virtual knots from real measurements.

(5) Remaining novelty space. I found no paper that:
- claims and proves EXACT invariance to lossless virtual-knot refinement for a model whose nonlinear layers are deep;
- pairs a learned diagonal SSM stem integrated in closed form over a piecewise-linear reconstruction with a clock τ_j = jΔ_c that is independent of the observations (arbitrary, non-integer, irregular);
- explicitly separates lossless refinement, real downsampling/aliasing and missing observations.
Framing must stay narrow. The general "multirate SSM" and "exact FOH" ideas are taken.

(6) Calibration numbers. No HAR (UCI) numbers appeared in this angle.
- SC10 raw (S4 table, reused by eSSM): S4 98.32 at 16 kHz → 96.30 zero-shot at 8 kHz; eSSM 97.59 → 94.23.

papers.title: Representation Equivalent Neural Operators: a Framework for Alias-free Operator Learning
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; 2 (WSK sampling, Def 2.1/2.2, CDE); 3.1-3.4 (Def 3.1, Example 3.2, Def 3.3, Def 3.4, Remark 3.5, Prop 3.6-3.8); 4 (CNN, FNO, CNO); 5.1-5.2 (incl. Table 1); 6; App A.1-A.3, B.1, B.2, C.1-C.3
papers.mechanism: This is a framework, not an architecture. It defines operator aliasing eps(U,u,Psi,Phi) = U - T_Phi o u o T_Psi^dagger and a representation-equivalence error tau(u,u'). A ReNO has zero aliasing for every admissible pair of input/output frame sequences, so its discrete versions at different discretizations are exactly equivalent (Prop 3.6), and composing ReNO layers gives a ReNO (Prop 3.7). The paper shows that FNO's pointwise activation breaks continuous-discrete equivalence (CDE), while CNO's upsample-sigma-downsample activation keeps it (B.2).
papers.input_reconstruction: Frame synthesis T_Psi. Examples use sinc and Dirichlet-kernel frames (band-limited interpolation); the theory allows any frame. Reconstruction is exact when the input lies in the frame's span.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: FNO and CNN apply sigma pointwise on the input grid. The ReNO-compliant fix evaluates the nonlinearity on a finer grid: a 2x output grid in Example 3.2, or CNO's upsampled band-limited grid, then projects back.
papers.time_handling: None. Spatial (PDE) setting; changing the discretization means changing the frame (grid resolution).
papers.invariance_claim: Exact representation equivalence (zero aliasing, tau = 0) between any two discretizations whose frames span the input and output spaces. For eps-ReNOs, tau is bounded by 2 eps sqrt(B_Psi)/sqrt(A_Phi). The paper contrasts this with the asymptotic 'discretization invariance' of Kovachki et al. Empirically, CNN and FNO are not equivalent, while CNO is error-free inside the 'equivalence zone'.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Trained on a 61-point grid (K=30 band-limited periodic functions) and tested on 2M+1-point grids: above Nyquist (lossless change of representation, a frame exists) and below Nyquist (information loss). No irregular or missing data.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 4 (FNO): "However the pointwise activation function sigma(f), applied to a bandlimited input f in B_Omega will not necessarily respect the bandlimits, i.e., sigma(f) not in B_Omega."
Sec. 3.1, Example 3.2 (|f|^2): "we can rectify this by sampling the output functions on a grid with twice the resolution of the input grid."
Remark 3.5: "Note that to avoid any aliasing error, the discrete representation of U has to depend on the chosen frame sequences, i.e. inevitably, u must depend on Psi and Phi"

Sec. 3.2 (before Prop 3.6): "while this concept establishes an asymptotic consistency, representation equivalence includes the direct comparison between any two given discretizations and guarantees their equivalence."

Fig. 2 caption: "The 'Resolution Equivalence' zone ... denotes the region where discrete representations have an associated frame, while the left-hand side represents the area where this is no longer the case (loss of input/output information)"
Sec. 3.3: "if each hidden layer in the operator (3.4) has an aliasing error (2.2), then these errors may propagate through the network and increase with increasing number of layers."
papers.reported_numbers: Table 1 (FNOs trained with a representation-equivalence penalty): representation-equivalence error 10.38/20.24/42.97/98.55% against translation-equivariance error 10.54/20.54/45.79/104.44%. No HAR, EigenWorms, SC or PDM numbers.
papers.code_url_and_license: No code URL found in the paper text.
papers.notes: This is the closest formal statement of the N2 principle, in operator learning. The framework covers arbitrary frames with nested spans. In principle that includes N2's lossless knot refinement: take the input frames to be linear B-spline (hat) functions on nested knot sets and represent the output on the fixed clock tau_j. N2 should therefore present its exact refinement invariance as an instance of ReNO-type representation equivalence for FOH/piecewise-linear frames, not as a new principle. ReNO does not treat time series, causal SSMs, non-uniform knots, closed-form exponential integration, or missing observations.

papers.title: Convolutional Neural Operators for robust and accurate learning of PDEs
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; 2 (setting, bandlimited approximation, convolution, up/downsampling, activation layer Eq. 2.6, U-Net, Prop 2.1); App A.4 (discrete operators); C.4 (testing at different resolutions); start of C.5 (ablation)
papers.mechanism: An operator U-Net on band-limited functions. Convolutions use discrete kernels on a predefined computational grid; up- and downsampling use (windowed) sinc filters. The activation layer is Sigma = D o sigma o U: upsample by N=2, apply sigma pointwise, sinc low-pass and downsample. Prop 2.1 proves CNO is a ReNO. For an input at another resolution, the input is first resampled to the fixed computational grid, the model is applied, and the output is resampled back.
papers.input_reconstruction: Band-limited interpolation with Kaiser-windowed sinc. An input with s' < s is upsampled; one with s' > s is low-pass filtered and downsampled to the computational grid.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: On a fixed computational grid that does not depend on the input resolution, at 2x upsampled resolution inside each activation layer.
papers.time_handling: None. Spatial 2D PDEs; resolution is the sampling rate s >= 2w.
papers.invariance_claim: In theory exact (ReNO/CDE) for band-limited inputs (Prop 2.1). The implementation uses windowed sinc, so it is approximate. Empirically 'approximately invariant to resolution' on Navier-Stokes.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Navier-Stokes data generated at 128x128, with lower resolutions obtained by downsampling. Models trained at 64x64 and tested across resolutions. FNO and UNet were applied directly to unresized inputs.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 2, Activation Layer: "Naively, one can apply the activation function pointwise to any function. However, it is well-known that such an application will no longer respect the band-limits of the underlying function space and generate aliasing errors"
Sec. 2, Eq. 2.6: "we first upsample the input function f in B_w to a higher bandlimit w_bar > w, then apply the activation and finally downsample the result back to the original bandlimit w"
App. C.4: "It is important to note that the implemented CNO models are specified on a predefined computational grid with a sampling rate of s >= 2w."
App. C.4: "If s' <= s, the signal needs to be upsampled to the sampling rate s by using an appropriate upsampling filter. However, if s' > s, it is necessary to filter out frequencies above s/2"
App. A.4 (activation layer): "In our experiments, we noticed that N=2 is sufficient for accurate predictions."
App. C.4: "The CNO model demonstrates the highest stability when it comes to resolution changes and is (approximately) invariant to resolution"
papers.reported_numbers: The cross-resolution result is only a figure (Fig. 2 right, Navier-Stokes); no numbers extracted. No HAR, EigenWorms, SC or PDM numbers.
papers.notes: CNO's cross-resolution protocol is exactly 'fixed-grid resampling + network', i.e. N2's mandatory baseline, with an anti-aliased nonlinearity added. For band-limited inputs it is exactly invariant to lossless refinement. It separates s' < s from s' > s, but does not treat irregular or missing samples or causal time.

papers.title: Alias-Free Generative Adversarial Networks (StyleGAN3)
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; 2 (continuous interpretation, Eq. 1); 2.1 (convolution, up/downsampling, nonlinearity); 3.2 (configs e, f, g)
papers.mechanism: Feature maps are treated as band-limited continuous signals that the samples only encode, so each discrete layer must implement a continuous operation that stays within the output bandlimit. The nonlinearity is wrapped as m-times upsample, leaky ReLU, low-pass filter and downsample (a custom CUDA kernel), with Kaiser-windowed sinc filters and non-critical sampling.
papers.input_reconstruction: Whittaker-Shannon (ideal sinc) interpolation, approximated with Kaiser-windowed sinc filters.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: On a temporary 2x upsampled grid of each layer's own sampling rate, which is fixed per layer in the generator.
papers.time_handling: None (images); each layer has a sampling rate s.
papers.invariance_claim: Continuous translation (and rotation) equivariance, approximate and measured empirically (EQ-T/EQ-R). There is no claim about sampling rate or resolution.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Sub-pixel translations and rotations of the generated image. No change of input resolution, no irregular sampling.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 1: "We identify two sources for it: 1) faint after-images of the pixel grid resulting from non-ideal upsampling filters ... and 2) the pointwise application of nonlinearities such as ReLU [60] or swish [47]."
Sec. 2.1, Nonlinearity: "Applying a pointwise nonlinearity sigma in the discrete domain does not commute with fractional translation or rotation."
Sec. 2.1, Nonlinearity: "We approximate this by upsampling the signal, applying the nonlinearity in the higher resolution, and downsampling it afterwards."
Sec. 2: "we shall interpret z(x) as being the actual signal being operated on, and the discretely sampled feature map Z[x] as merely a convenient encoding for it."
Sec. 3.2, config f: "In practice, we find m=2 to be sufficient (Figure 3, right), again improving EQ-T (config f)."
papers.reported_numbers: None relevant (FID and EQ-T only; not extracted).
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/NVlabs/stylegan3; NVIDIA Source Code License for StyleGAN3 (LICENSE.txt header checked).
papers.notes: This is where the filtered (upsample-sigma-downsample) nonlinearity used by CNO and MambaNO comes from. The mechanism is the one N2 relies on: a pointwise sigma generates content that later linear operators read differently depending on the grid. The goal here, however, is geometric equivariance, not consistency across sampling rates.

papers.title: Alias-Free Mamba Neural Operator
papers.arxiv_or_venue: NeurIPS 2024 (read from the proceedings PDF); arXiv id unknown
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 2.2 (alias-free framework); 3 (Eqs. 3.9-3.19, Algorithm 1, MambaNO architecture, Prop 3.1); 4.3 (resolution invariance); App A.1; ZOH derivation Eqs. A.9-A.13; App B.2 (ReNO proof)
papers.mechanism: A U-shaped neural operator that combines local convolution integration with a 'Mamba integration' SSM, derived from a kernel integral with kernel C e^{A(x-y)} B and scanned in four directions. It uses CNO-style alias-free activations D o sigma o U and sinc up/downsampling. The SSM is discretized with ZOH / Scharfetter-Gummel: A_bar = exp(Delta A), B_bar = (Delta A)^{-1}(exp(Delta A) - I) Delta B, where Delta, B and C are Linear(v), i.e. computed from the input.
papers.input_reconstruction: Sinc (band-limited) frames between layers. Inside the SSM, a ZOH assumption: v is taken as constant on [x_k, x_{k+1}].
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Activations run on an upsampled band-limited grid (as in CNO). The selective SSM, however, computes Delta, B and C from v at every grid point, i.e. per-sample and input-dependent.
papers.time_handling: Spatial scan index, with timescale Delta used as the step size. No physical time.
papers.invariance_claim: Claims MambaNO is a ReNO (Prop 3.1) with 'little aliasing errors'. The proof in B.2 treats the SSM output as a global LTI convolution kernel K_bar mapping B_w to B_w. Empirically, error is flat across resolutions on Navier-Stokes.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Navier-Stokes at several test resolutions (CNO protocol). No irregular sampling.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 3 (activation operators): "As known, applying the activation function point-wise directly would break the band-limits of the underlying function space, potentially introducing arbitrarily higher-frequency information and causing aliasing errors"
Algorithm 1 (SSM Block), line 1: "Delta,B,C = Linear(v), Linear(v), Linear(v)"
Appendix, before Eq. A.12: "According to the concept of zero-order hold, when Delta approaches 0, we can regard the value of function v in the interval [xk,xk+1] as a constant v(xk+1)"
Prop. 3.1: "Mamba Neural Operator G : B_w(D,R^dX) -> B_w(D,R^dY) is a Representation equivalent Neural Operator (ReNO). That is, MambaNO enjoys the CDE property."
App. B.2: "the output of the mamba integration (also known as SSM) can be defined as a global convolution integral like Eq. (3.15)."
papers.reported_numbers: None relevant (resolution result is a plot only).
papers.code_url_and_license: Not found in the extracted text.
papers.notes: This is the most direct 'SSM + alias-free' predecessor. It keeps ZOH with Delta as the step size and computes the input-dependent Delta, B, C at every grid point. Its ReNO proof models the SSM as an LTI convolution and does not address this per-sample selectivity, so an N2-style counterexample (a selective gate evaluated per observation) is not covered by that proof. Not time series; no FOH; no exact integration.

papers.title: Spectral Neural Operators
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1 (incl. Fig. 1 caption); 2; 3.1 (activation functions and aliasing, Theorem 1); 3.2 (super-resolution); 4 (definition of SNO, Eq. 3); end of App A (grid-refinement variant, Eq. 16)
papers.mechanism: A neural operator that maps a fixed number of Chebyshev or Fourier coefficients of the input to a fixed number of output coefficients (any network from C^n to C^m). Input coefficients come from grid samples via DCT/FFT, with series chopping if the input does not fit the architecture. Evaluation on finer grids uses spectral interpolation, kept separate from the learned map.
papers.input_reconstruction: Chebyshev or trigonometric (spectral) interpolation; exact for truncated series.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: On the fixed coefficient vector (or the corresponding fixed grid) of the architecture, independent of the input grid.
papers.time_handling: None; spatial/temporal PDE axes are treated as function domains, with no dt.
papers.invariance_claim: Claims SNO 'never suffers from aliasing', exact for inputs in the truncated-series class. Shows that FNO outputs on grids h and 2h differ by about 25% in L2, because the activation aliases. Argues that refining the grid of a fully resolved function adds no information.
papers.grid_changes_tested: FNO trained on grid 2h and evaluated on grid h: lossless refinement of trigonometric polynomials. Also an improved super-resolution test that adds higher harmonics on a finer grid, i.e. new information.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 1: "For FNO situation is more difficult, because even when the input function is fully resolved, nonlinear activations are going to introduce higher frequencies, so the lower frequencies will be distorted."
Sec. 3.1: "If all operations are poinwise as in case of DeepONet or PiNN, it is not problematic. However, for FNO which uses global information, aliasing will present a problem."
Sec. 3.1: "Our solution to the problem of aliasing errors is to decouple interpolation from the mapping between functional spaces."

Sec. 3.2: "If we sample these functions on the uniform grid with 2N+1 points, we can exactly recover all 2N+1 coefficients and no further refinement of the grid is going to provide novel information about the function"
Fig. 1 caption: "The average discrepancy is about 25% of L2 norm. Inconsistency of FNO results from aliasing of high harmonics produced by activation functions."
Abstract: "The resulting Spectral Neural Operator (SNO) has transparent output, never suffers from aliasing, and may include many exact (lossless) operations on functions."
papers.reported_numbers: FNO trained on grid 2h and evaluated on h: average discrepancy about 25% of L2 norm (derivative task, Fig. 1b). On finer grids, FNO test error is about 2x larger for integration and 5x for differentiation (Sec. 3.1). No HAR, EigenWorms, SC or PDM numbers.
papers.notes: This is the earliest explicit statement found of N2's core observation, together with its fix: under lossless refinement, a pointwise sigma followed by a global linear operator makes the output grid-dependent; the fix is a fixed-size representation in which the nonlinearity does not depend on the input grid. SNO also states the key nuance: purely pointwise pipelines are unaffected. The dependence appears only when sigma-outputs feed a global or integral operator, which is exactly the case of sigma-outputs feeding the next SSM layer.

papers.title: Discretization-invariance? On the Discretization Mismatch Errors in Neural Operators (CROP)
papers.sections_read: ICLR virtual-poster abstract; official GitHub README (Introduction and 'Community Findings'); third-party description in Sakarvadia et al. 2025 (arXiv 2510.06646) Sec. 4.2. The paper body was NOT read (OpenReview PDF returned 403).
papers.mechanism: Defines the discretization mismatch error (DME): the difference between a neural operator's outputs for the same input at different discretizations. Bounds it: the DME grows with test resolution and accumulates across layers and autoregressive steps. CROP lifts the input into band-limited latent functions whose discretization is fixed at one resolution. Any intermediate network (FNO, CNO's U-Net without anti-alias activation, a CNN) runs at that fixed resolution, and the result is projected back.
papers.input_reconstruction: Band-limited lifting / interpolation to a fixed-dimensional representation (exact filters not read).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At the fixed intermediate resolution, independent of the input resolution.
papers.time_handling: Spatial PDEs, plus autoregressive rollout for time-dependent PDEs (not dt-based).
papers.invariance_claim: README: the intermediate layers introduce no DME and no aliasing error, provided the latent space is band-limited. The exact conditions were not verified from the paper.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Train at one resolution, test at higher and lower ones (README table: Navier-Stokes at 32-256, trained at 64).
evidence_quotes: README Introduction: "We define discretization mismatch errors (DMEs) in Sec. 4.1 as the difference between the neural operator outputs when taking the same input at different discretizations."

README: "Since the latent feature functions reside in a bandlimited function space, we can fix the resolution of their discretized forms within the limits tolerated by the bandlimits. As a result, no discretization mismatch errors are introduced by the intermediate layers."
README: "Given a fixed training resolution and a higher testing resolution, we show that the DME increases as the testing resolution increases."

README (author's additional insights): "The instability of grid-based neural operators across resolutions, including FNO, largely arises from non-linear activation functions, and the linear layers further amplify this instability."

Sakarvadia et al. 2025, Sec. 4.2, describing CROP: "extends to any class of model by interpolating inputs (both at training and inference) to and from a fixed-dimensional representation before and after a forward pass."
papers.reported_numbers: README community table (Navier-Stokes, trained at 64), L2 error at 256/128/64/32: post-Dec-2022 FNO 0.0618/0.0420/0.00856/0.0869; CROP + post-Dec-2022 FNO 0.00636/0.00636/0.00636/0.00635. No HAR or SC numbers.
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/wenhangao21/ICLR25-CROP; no LICENSE file at the repo root (main or master checked).
papers.notes: A very close conceptual match to N2's rule: run nonlinear updates only on a fixed grid, so the intermediate representation does not depend on the discretization. Spatial domain, band-limited rather than FOH, no exact integration. The paper body was not read; the OpenReview PDF should be checked before any claim relative to CROP is finalized.

papers.title: The False Promise of Zero-Shot Super-Resolution in Machine-Learned Operators
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 3.1 (resolution interpolation / information extrapolation); 3.2; 4 (4.1, 4.2 band-limited learning: CNO, CROP); App K (anti-alias nonlinearities); App M (downsampling methods)
papers.mechanism: An empirical study of FNO, CNO and CROP across resolutions. Multi-resolution inference is split into 'resolution interpolation' (same frequency content, different sampling rate) and 'information extrapolation' (new frequency content at a fixed rate). The authors propose multi-resolution training as the remedy.
papers.input_reconstruction: Low-pass filter then downsample (for resolution interpolation). App M compares strided, average-pooling and bilinear downsampling.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: FNO: pointwise on the input grid; also FNO with anti-alias (up-sigma-down) activations. CNO and CROP: at a fixed resolution.
papers.time_handling: Spatial PDEs; autoregressive time steps for Navier-Stokes.
papers.invariance_claim: Negative and empirical. FNO fails at both resolution interpolation and extrapolation. CNO does not alias but cannot predict frequencies beyond its training band. Anti-alias activations do not fix data-driven aliasing.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Resolution interpolation with fixed low-pass content (a lossless-type change); information extrapolation; joint super- and sub-resolution; strided downsampling as a model of real measurements.
evidence_quotes: Abstract: "We decouple multi-resolution inference into two key behaviors: 1) extrapolation to varying frequency information; and 2) interpolating across varying resolutions."
Sec. 3.1 (Resolution Interpolation): "we keep the set of populated frequencies constant in the train and test data, while varying the resolution of the test data."

Sec. 4.2: "CNOs are fixed-resolution models; to use them, one must first interpolate their input to the model's training resolution, do a forward pass, and then interpolate back to the original dimension."
Sec. 4.2: "This means that while CNO does not alias, it cannot predict frequencies higher than what was seen during training."

App. M: "strided downsampling ... simulates realistic experimental settings in which you have measurements of a system at fixed intervals and no method to resolve intermediate points between intervals"
papers.reported_numbers: Losses vary by 1x, 2x and 10x across test resolutions for Darcy, Burgers and Navier-Stokes respectively (Sec. 3.2, Fig. 16). No HAR or SC numbers.
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/msakarvadia/operator_aliasing; a LICENSE file exists but contains placeholder text, so the license type could not be identified.
papers.notes: Their split between resolution interpolation and information extrapolation is the spatial analogue of N2's knot refinement versus real downsampling; missing observations are not treated. They show that fixed-grid band-limited methods (CNO, CROP) remove aliasing but cannot add information, which supports N2's rule of not promising aliasing recovery.

papers.title: Limits of Resolution Equivariance in Fourier Neural Operators
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; 2 (methodology, inference protocols, Eq. 1); 3 (results and analysis); 4 (discussion); i.e. the entire main text
papers.mechanism: Compares two inference protocols: Direct-S (run the FNO on the fine grid) and Low+pad, y = U_{s->S}(M(T_{S->s}(x_S))): Fourier-truncate the input to the training grid, run the model there, and zero-pad the output. This is done in a best-case band-limited setting where the extra fine-grid modes are zero, together with layerwise spectral measurements.
papers.input_reconstruction: Fourier truncation and Fourier zero-padding (band-limited).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: FNO's GeLU is applied pointwise on whichever grid the model runs. The baseline keeps it on the training grid.
papers.time_handling: None (Darcy flow).
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical: direct fine-grid inference is not reliably beneficial and can be worse than Low+pad, even when the input carries no new frequencies. Because the linear parts of FNO act mode-wise, the mismatch is attributed primarily to the nonlinearities.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Train at s=85 and test at S > s (e.g. 211), with band-limited (Fourier-padded) inputs, which is the analogue of lossless refinement.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 3: "We therefore focus on a controlled best-case setting where the additional high-frequency modes at S are set to zero via Fourier padding"

Sec. 3: "Because the linear parts of FNO (spectral convolution and residual linear map) are mode-wise, these resolution-dependent spectral corruption points to the nonlinearities (and their discretization) as the primary source of the mismatch."

Sec. 2: "This baseline cannot recover frequencies outside the training band, but it avoids executing the network at an unseen discretization and provides a strong reference for cross-resolution evaluation."
Abstract: "Our findings highlight a simple but strong baseline for cross-resolution evaluation and point to nonlinear aliasing as a key obstacle to zero-shot resolution equivariance."
papers.reported_numbers: Figures only; no numbers.
papers.code_url_and_license: Uses the official FNO implementation; no code URL of their own found.
papers.notes: This is essentially N2's 'minimal counterexample' (lossless refinement plus a pointwise sigma gives a different output), shown empirically for FNO in 2026. It also shows the fixed-grid baseline (run at the training resolution) beating direct execution. N2 must cite it and must not claim this diagnosis as new.

papers.title: Principled Approaches for Extending Neural Architectures to Function Spaces for Operator Learning
papers.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv 2506.10973 (Berner, Liu-Schiaffini, Kossaifi, Duruisseaux, Bonev, Azizzadenesheli, Anandkumar)
papers.sections_read: 3.2 (elementwise functions to pointwise operators); parts of 3.3; 3.6 (encoders and decoders, Eq. 15); 3.7 (interpolation); 5.2 (interpolation, multi-resolution training); summary lines
papers.mechanism: A survey/tutorial of recipes for turning neural-network layers into discretization-agnostic operator layers: integral transforms with quadrature, pointwise (Nemytskii) operators, spectral convolutions, encoders and decoders built from inner products or projections, and interpolation to a fixed latent grid.
papers.input_reconstruction: Quadrature-weighted inner products; spline, kernel or Fourier interpolation (bilinear in their experiments).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: In general pointwise at the input points; alternatively inside a network applied on a fixed latent discretization after interpolation.
papers.time_handling: None (spatial).
papers.invariance_claim: Discretization convergence, i.e. asymptotic. Notes that interpolating to a fixed resolution defines a neural operator that generalizes across resolutions but throws away high-resolution information.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Navier-Stokes trained at 128 and tested at other resolutions; mixed-resolution training; U-Net with input/output interpolation.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 3.2: "Operations that are applied pointwise to the discretized function are naturally agnostic to the resolution. This includes activation functions as well as liftings and projections. However, they can be queried only at the input points."
Sec. 3.7: "one can interpolate the input discretization to a latent, fixed discretization, apply a neural network, and then interpolate its output to allow querying at arbitrary points."
Sec. 5.2 (Interpolation): "its performance is limited since it discards any high-resolution information in the input."
Sec. 3.6, Eq. 15 (inner-product encoder): "v_j = sum_i [b_j(x_i)]* f(x_i) Delta_i ~ integral [b_j(x)]* f(x) dx = <b_j, f>"
papers.reported_numbers: None relevant.
papers.notes: Documents 'interpolate to a fixed latent grid, then run a network' as a standard construction (this is N2's mandatory baseline) and the quadrature-approximated inner-product encoder. N2's exact stem is an exact, closed-form version of such an encoder, using an exponential kernel against the FOH path and read out on a fixed clock.

papers.title: Discretization Error of Fourier Neural Operators
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; 1.1; 1.2 (related work); 3 (Assumptions 3.1, Theorems 3.2 and 3.3, Remark 3.4, Lemma 3.5)
papers.mechanism: Bounds the discretization (aliasing) error between the continuum FNO and its grid implementation: ||v_t - v_t^N|| <= C N^{-s} for smooth activations and H^s inputs. Also proposes adaptive subsampling during training.
papers.input_reconstruction: Grid samples; a trigonometric interpolant is used for the continuum comparison.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Pointwise on the N-point grid (as in the implemented FNO).
papers.time_handling: None.
papers.invariance_claim: Only an asymptotic convergence rate N^{-s}; no invariance at finite N.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Varying N for random-weight and trained FNOs.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 1: "during a forward pass of the FNO, the aliasing error propagates through the subsequent model layers and may be amplified by nonlinearities."
Sec. 3: "we show that the approximate L2 norm of the error after any number of layers decreases like N^{-s}, where s describes the Sobolev regularity of the input."
Sec. 1.2: "Convolutional Neural Operators (CNO), which are not strictly alias free, but reduce aliasing errors via spatial upsampling [22]."
papers.reported_numbers: None relevant.
papers.notes: An example of the existing discretization-error inequalities that N2 must label as prior results: the error from evaluating the nonlinearity on the grid is known to vanish only asymptotically.

papers.title: Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations
papers.sections_read: Read by keyword extraction: Sec. 1 contributions; Sec. 3 (iterative update definition); Sec. 4 'Invariance to discretization'; Sec. 5 'Remark on Resolution'; 5.4 zero-shot super-resolution
papers.mechanism: Layers v_{t+1} = sigma(W v_t + K v_t), where K is a Fourier multiplier on truncated modes, implemented with an FFT on the input grid.
papers.input_reconstruction: Samples on a uniform grid; trigonometric interpolation implied by the DFT.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Pointwise at every point of the input grid.
papers.time_handling: Time is either an extra spatial dimension (FNO-3D) or handled autoregressively; no dt adaptation.
papers.invariance_claim: Claims discretization invariance, a 'resolution-invariant solution operator' and zero-shot super-resolution; informal and empirical.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Trained at 64x64x20 and evaluated at 256x256x80 (Navier-Stokes); Burgers and Darcy at several resolutions.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 4, Invariance to discretization: "The Fourier layers are discretization-invariant because they can learn from and evaluate functions which are discretized in an arbitrary way."
Sec. 3: "In each iteration, the update v_t -> v_{t+1} is defined as the composition of a non-local integral operator K and a local, nonlinear activation function sigma."
Sec. 5.4: "it can be trained on a lower resolution and evaluated at a higher resolution, without seeing any higher resolution data (zero-shot super-resolution)."
papers.reported_numbers: None relevant.
papers.notes: This is the claim that SNO, ReNO, CROP, Sakarvadia and Colagrande later refute. The pattern (linear part discretization-agnostic, sigma on the input grid) is the spatial equivalent of N2's 'step-size rescaling only' case.

papers.title: Neural Operator: Learning Maps Between Function Spaces
papers.sections_read: Read by keyword extraction: Abstract; Sec. 1 'Discretization-Invariant Models'; Definition 4; layer Eq. (general iterative layer); Sec. 8.2 Theorem 8 statement
papers.mechanism: General neural operator: lifting, iterated layers sigma(W v + integral kappa v dnu + b), then projection. The integral operators are discretized by quadrature / Riemann sums.
papers.input_reconstruction: Point evaluations; integrals approximated by Riemann sums.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Pointwise (Nemytskii) at the discretization points of each layer domain D_t. The layer domains are hyperparameters; in practice they are the input grid.
papers.time_handling: None.
papers.invariance_claim: Asymptotic only: the model converges to a continuum operator as the discretization is refined (Def. 4, Thm 8).
papers.grid_changes_tested: Refinement experiments showing roughly constant error.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 1, Discretization-Invariant Models, requirement 3: "converges to a continuum operator as the discretization is refined."

Sec. 8.2: "The proof, provided in appendix E, constructs a sequence of finite dimensional maps which approximate the neural operator by Riemann sums and shows uniform converges of the error over compact sets"

Sec. 1: "families of graph neural networks ... and transformer models ... are resolution invariant, i.e., they can receive inputs at any resolution, but they fail to converge to a continuum operator as discretization is refined."
papers.reported_numbers: None relevant.
papers.notes: Defines the asymptotic notion of discretization invariance that ReNO, and N2's exact finite-grid invariance, are contrasted with.

papers.title: CKConv: Continuous Kernel Convolution For Sequential Data
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; 4.1 (properties, incl. data at different resolutions); 5 (tests at different sampling rates, irregular data, Tables 4-5); App A.1, A.2, E.2, E.3
papers.mechanism: Convolution kernels are continuous functions of relative position (a SIREN MLP). At a new sampling rate, the kernel is sampled on the new grid and rescaled by sr2/sr1; when the test rate is higher, the kernel is Gaussian-blurred first.
papers.input_reconstruction: None: samples are used directly, as a Riemann-sum approximation of the continuous convolution.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Pointwise at every input sample, between layers (standard CNN blocks).
papers.time_handling: Relative positions normalized to [-1,1]; kernel resampled at the sampling rate, with a normalization factor.
papers.invariance_claim: Approximate: (x*psi)_{sr2} ~ (sr2/sr1)(x*psi)_{sr1}, via Riemann sums (App. A.2). Empirically stable.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Different train/test rates by subsampling seq[::n] (real downsampling) on CharacterTrajectories and raw Speech Commands (SC_raw). Random drops of 30/50/70% (missing data) on CT, SC_raw and PhysioNet.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 4.1: "That is, convolutions calculated at different resolutions sr1 and sr2 are approximately equal up to a factor given by the resolution change."
App. E.2: "subsampling by a factor n is performed by running seq[::n]."

App. E.3: "our continuous kernels often contain frequency components of frequency higher than the resolution of the sampling grid used during training (Fig. 9). As these high-frequency components are not observed during training, we observe that they hurt performance"
papers.reported_numbers: SC_raw (16 kHz, 10 classes), CKCNN with 100k parameters (Table 5). Trained at 1, tested at 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16: 71.66 / 65.96 / 52.11 / 40.33 / 30.87. Trained at 1/2, tested at 1, 1/2, 1/4: 72.09 / 72.06 / 69.03. Trained at 1/4, tested at 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16: 68.25 / 68.40 / 69.47 / 67.09 / 37.91. CharacterTrajectories, trained at 1, tested at 1/2: 99.30. Missing data (Table 4) at 0/30/50/70% drop: SC_raw 71.66 / 63.46 / 60.55 / 57.50; CT 99.53 / 99.30 / 98.83 / 98.14.
papers.notes: A resolution-agnostic linear operator with per-sample nonlinearities, which is the configuration N2 targets. It tests real downsampling and missing data separately, but has no notion of lossless refinement.

papers.title: FlexConv: Continuous Kernel Convolutions with Differentiable Kernel Sizes
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; 3.3 (analytic alias-free MAGNets); 4.3 (alias-free FlexNets); 6 (limitations); overview of App A
papers.mechanism: Continuous kernels of learnable size, parameterized by MAGNets. The kernel's maximum frequency is derived analytically and regularized to stay below the Nyquist frequency of the training resolution, so kernels can be resampled at higher resolutions.
papers.input_reconstruction: None.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Pointwise (ReLU etc.) at every input pixel or sequence step.
papers.time_handling: Kernel resampled on a denser grid.
papers.invariance_claim: Approximate (Eq. 9 holds approximately); empirically 'minimal accuracy loss' when deployed at a higher resolution.
papers.grid_changes_tested: CIFAR-10 source/target resolution pairs (e.g. 16 to 32, test data upsampled); ImageNet-k.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 3.3: "Note however, that Eq. 9 holds approximately. This is due to aliasing artifacts which can appear if the frequencies in the learned kernel surpass the Nyquist criterion of the target resolution."

Sec. 6 (Limitations): "Some drop in accuracy is still observed when using alias-free FlexNets at a higher test resolutions (Tab. 4). Although more evidence is needed, this may be caused by aliasing effects introduced by ReLU (Vasconcelos et al., 2021)"
papers.reported_numbers: CIFAR/ImageNet-k only; not extracted.
papers.notes: Explicitly conjectures that the per-sample nonlinearity is the remaining source of resolution dependence after the kernels are anti-aliased, which is the N2 question, but offers no fix.

papers.title: Towards a General Purpose CNN for Long Range Dependencies in ND (CCNN)
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; the paragraph on continuous kernels / 'Equivalent responses across input resolutions'; App A (Speech Commands description); normalized relative positions paragraph
papers.mechanism: CKConv/FlexConv-style continuous kernels inside S4-like residual blocks, forming a single architecture for 1D and 2D data.
papers.input_reconstruction: None.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Pointwise at every input sample.
papers.time_handling: Kernel coordinates normalized to [-1,1] and resampled for the resolution.
papers.invariance_claim: Approximate equality of the convolution across resolutions, up to a scale factor (inherited from CKConv).
papers.grid_changes_tested: Mentions test-time resolution changes; no SC resolution-change numbers found in the text read.
evidence_quotes: 'Equivalent responses across input resolutions' paragraph: "For a signal x and a continuous convolutional kernel K sampled at resolutions r(1) and r(2), the convolution at both resolutions are approximately equal up to a factor proportional to the resolution change (Romero et al., 2022b)"
papers.reported_numbers: None on resolution change extracted.
papers.notes: Largely redundant with CKConv for this angle.

papers.title: S4ND: Modeling Images and Videos as Multidimensional Signals Using State Spaces
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; 4.2 (resolution change and bandlimiting); 5.3 (continuous-signal capabilities); App B.3.1
papers.mechanism: Multidimensional S4 kernels built as outer products of 1D SSM kernels. Resolution change is handled by scaling Delta; a bandlimiting mask zeroes the C coefficients of modes whose frequency exceeds alpha/2 of Nyquist.
papers.input_reconstruction: Only the implicit SSM discretization (ZOH/bilinear). Lower-resolution images are made by antialiased bilinear resizing.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Pointwise at every pixel / grid point (standard isotropic and ConvNeXt backbones).
papers.time_handling: Delta rescaled by the resolution ratio.
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical zero-shot resolution change; no exactness claim.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Train at low or mid resolution (antialiased bilinear downsampling), test at the base resolution; progressive resizing.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 4.2: "This capability relies simply on scaling Delta by the relative change in frequencies (i.e., if the input resolution is doubled, halve the SSM's Delta parameter)."

Sec. 1: "While S4ND can be used at any resolution, performance suffers when moving between resolutions due to aliasing artifacts in the kernel, an issue also noted by prior work on continuous models [50]."

App. B.3: "Images at the lower resolutions are generated by taking an image at the base resolution, and then downsampling using the resize function in torchvision, with bilinear interpolation and antialiasing turned on."

papers.notes: The canonical 'dt-only' approach. It addresses aliasing in the kernel only; the nonlinearities stay per-sample.

papers.title: State Space Models for Event Cameras
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1; 2.2; 3.1-3.3.2 (SSM-ViT block, output masking, H2 norm); 4.1; 4.3.3 (Table 5)
papers.mechanism: SSM-ViT blocks (convolution, block and grid attention, then an S4D/S5 temporal SSM whose state is carried across windows). Running at a higher frequency is done by scaling the timescale (rate r). Aliasing is countered by masking high-frequency modes of the output (alpha) or by an H2-norm penalty above omega_min.
papers.input_reconstruction: None: events are binned into dense tensors per window (50 ms, 10 bins).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Convolution, attention and MLP run on every window, i.e. at every observation step.
papers.time_handling: Delta scaled by the frequency ratio (dt-only).
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical: 'minimal performance degradation' at higher frequencies. No invariance claim.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Train at 20 Hz, test at 40, 80, 100 and 200 Hz. Smaller windows change the per-step input, so this is not the same reconstructed path.
evidence_quotes: Sec. 1: "This feature permits inference at arbitrary frequencies by globally adjusting the timescale parameter based on the ratio between the new and old frequency sampling rates."
Sec. 3.3: "It gives rise to the well-documented issue of aliasing [38, 37], which occurs when the kernel bandwidth surpasses the Nyquist frequency."
Sec. 4.1: "Event representations are formed based on 50 ms time windows that correspond to 20 Hz sampling frequency, divided into T = 10 discrete bins."
papers.notes: A dt-only baseline. N2's counterexample applies: the per-window nonlinear blocks change the representation with frequency even after Delta is scaled.

papers.title: Alias-Free Convnets: Fractional Shift Invariance via Polynomial Activations
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1 (polynomial activations, contributions); 2 (alias-free activation discussion, Algorithm 1); 3 (activation function implementation); App B.1
papers.mechanism: Degree-2 polynomial activations applied after upsampling by (d+1)/2, followed by an ideal low-pass filter and downsampling. Together with alias-free LayerNorm and BlurPool this gives a CNN that is provably shift-invariant, including for fractional shifts.
papers.input_reconstruction: Ideal sinc interpolation.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: On a 2x upsampled grid of each layer (for d = 2). This is exact because a degree-d polynomial expands the bandwidth by exactly a factor d.
papers.time_handling: None.
papers.invariance_claim: Exact (certified) shift invariance and equivariance for circular fractional shifts with ideal sinc interpolation; empirical for other shifts.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Sub-pixel and crop/interpolated translations; no resolution change.
evidence_quotes: Abstract: "The existing architectural solutions to prevent aliasing are partial since they do not solve these effects, that originate in non-linearities."
Sec. 2: "For example, the outputs of non-differentiable operations such as ReLU can have infinite support in the frequency domain, thus aliasing will be induced for every finite upsampling factor."
Sec. 1 (Contributions): "Specifically, the robustness of AFCs is certified for circular shifts and the ideal (Sinc) interpolation kernel."
Sec. 3 (Activation function): "We replace the original GeLU activation with a polynomial function of degree 2, whose coefficients are trainable parameters, per channel"
papers.reported_numbers: None relevant.
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/hmichaeli/alias_free_convnets; repo license not verified (the repo contains a ConvNeXt license file).
papers.notes: Shows that an exactly alias-free nonlinearity is possible only for nonlinearities that expand bandwidth by a finite factor (polynomials). N2 avoids band-limit assumptions altogether by fixing the clock instead of making sigma alias-free.

papers.title: Sampling-Frequency-Independent Audio Source Separation Using Convolution Layer Based on Impulse Invariant Method
papers.sections_read: Abstract; I; III-A; III-B; III-C; IV-A; IV-B; V
papers.mechanism: Conv-TasNet in which the encoder convolution (and decoder transposed convolution) weights are generated from latent analog filters (trainable multi-phase gammatone) by impulse invariance, h[l] = T g(lT), for the input sampling period T. Kernel size L and stride W are scaled with the sampling frequency fs so that frame length and hop stay fixed in seconds. The nonlinear mask predictor is unchanged. Channels whose centre frequency is above Nyquist are zeroed.
papers.input_reconstruction: None explicit: discrete FIR filtering of the samples, with the analog filter sampled (an approximation).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: The encoder ReLU and the entire mask predictor run on a frame sequence whose hop is fixed in physical time (2.5 ms). This is a fixed physical-time clock for any input fs, as long as W comes out as an integer.
papers.time_handling: Filters parameterized in continuous time; stride scaled with fs so the physical frame rate is constant.
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical: SDR stays consistent from 12 to 48 kHz after training at 16 kHz. No exactness claim.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Test tracks resampled (down and up) to 8-48 kHz.
evidence_quotes: Sec. III-C: "we determine L and W for each target sampling frequency to keep the frame length and shift unchanged in the continuous time domain."
Sec. III-C: "Hence, as the sampling frequency doubles, L and W should double to make the representation consistent for the masking module."
Sec. III-A, Eq. 2: "The impulse invariant method generates a discrete-time impulse response h[l] from an analog filter g(t) so that the sampled instants coincide: h[l]=Tg(lT)."
Sec. III-B: "we propose to set the weights of the mth channel to zero whenever the center frequency f_m of the corresponding analog filter is above the Nyquist frequency."
Sec. III-C: "By replacing all convolution layers in the masking modules with the SFI convolution layers, this issue might be resolved. However, we left it as a future work"
papers.reported_numbers: MUSDB18-HQ SDR shown in figures only; no numbers extracted. No HAR or SC numbers.
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/TomohikoNakamura/sfi_convtasnet (code for the 2022 TASLP journal version); MIT (LICENSE checked).
papers.notes: The closest time-domain precedent for N2's architecture: a linear front end that adapts to the sampling rate, feeding a nonlinear network on a fixed physical-time frame clock. Differences from N2: FIR/impulse-invariant approximation rather than exact integration; integer strides required (fixed by the 2023 follow-up); no FOH or closed-form SSM integration; no invariance claim under knot refinement; source separation rather than classification.

papers.title: Algorithms of Sampling-Frequency-Independent Layers for Non-integer Strides
papers.sections_read: Abstract; I; II-A, II-B, II-C; III-A, III-B, III-C; IV-A, IV-B, IV-C; V
papers.mechanism: When the stride S' = (T/T')S is not an integer, the convolution output y_c[i] is interpolated with a windowed sinc and sampled at times m S' T'. The mask predictor therefore always receives frames at the trained physical frame rate. The transposed convolution is handled the same way.
papers.input_reconstruction: Windowed-sinc interpolation (Kaiser window, L=16) of the intermediate linear features.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: ReLU and mask predictor run at fixed physical-time frame instants m S' T' (a fixed 2.5 ms hop).

angle_summary:
1) The N2 principle already exists in another domain. It has been stated and fixed in spatial operator learning:
- SNO (arXiv 2205.10573, 2022) says that refining the grid of a fully resolved function adds no information. It shows FNO outputs differ between grids h and 2h (about 25% L2) because the pointwise activation aliases. It notes the problem only appears when sigma-outputs feed a global or integral operator. Its fix is a fixed-size representation.
- ReNO (2305.19913) formalizes exact representation equivalence across discretizations and fixes Example 3.2 by evaluating the nonlinearity on a 2x output grid. Its 'equivalence zone' versus 'no-equivalence zone' already separates a lossless change of representation from information loss.
- CNO (2302.01178) resamples every input to one fixed computational grid and applies sigma on a 2x upsampled grid.
- CROP (ICLR 2025) fixes the intermediate resolution so hidden layers add no discretization mismatch error.
- Colagrande et al. (2606.00677, 2026) test a lossless, band-limited refinement and trace the mismatch mainly to the nonlinearities; the fixed-grid Low+pad baseline beats direct execution.
- Sakarvadia et al. (2510.06646) separate resolution interpolation (same content) from information extrapolation (new content).
- Berner et al. (2506.10973) present 'interpolate to a fixed latent grid, then run a network' as a standard construction.
- StyleGAN3 and Alias-Free Convnets use the same nonlinearity-aliasing mechanism, but for translation equivariance.
Rating: substantial overlap on the principle. N2 must cite these and present its invariance as an instance of ReNO-type representation equivalence for piecewise-linear/FOH frames.

2) A fixed physical-time clock for the nonlinear part already exists in time-domain audio. The SFI Conv-TasNet line (Saito 2021; Nakamura, TASLP 2022; Imamura, EUSIPCO 2023; a 2025 journal extension that could not be read) keeps a nonlinear mask predictor at a fixed physical frame rate. It is fed by a linear front end built from continuous-time filters (approximate impulse-invariant or frequency-domain design), with sinc interpolation for non-integer strides. Their stated reason: the mask predictor's input "should have the same time resolution for any SFs". They compare against resampling to the training rate and beat it at lower sampling rates.

3) The SSM and continuous-kernel papers (S4, S4ND, Zubic 2024, CKConv/FlexConv/CCNN, MambaNO) adapt only dt or the kernel sampling. They fight kernel aliasing (bandlimiting mask, H2 penalty, Gaussian blur) but leave the nonlinearities per-sample.
- FlexConv explicitly conjectures that the remaining resolution drop comes from ReLU aliasing.
- MambaNO claims ReNO while computing Delta, B, C from the input at every grid point; its proof treats the SSM as an LTI convolution. This gap could be a concrete N2 counterexample target.

4) Not found in this angle:
- closed-form integration of a piecewise-linear (FOH) input path by a continuous-time diagonal SSM on arbitrary non-uniform knots, giving exact invariance under virtual-knot insertion;
- a causal, fixed-clock SSM stack for time-series classification;
- an explicit three-way separation that includes missing observations.
Existing discretization-error bounds (Trautner/Lanthaler/Stuart N^{-s}; Kovachki's asymptotic definition) must be labelled as prior results.

5) Main risk, which the orchestrator should weigh. Resampling the same FOH interpolant to a fixed grid (point evaluation at tau_j) and then running an SSM is also exactly invariant to virtual-knot insertion, because the interpolant does not change. The CNO/CROP pipelines are exactly this. So refinement invariance cannot distinguish N2 from its mandatory baseline. Any N2 gain has to come from exact integration of the information between clock ticks (anti-aliasing, using all measurements) under real downsampling or irregular grids. Prior evidence shows fixed-grid resampling is a strong baseline (Kabri 2023; Colagrande 2026; CNO C.4), with SFI 2023 the counter-example where it degrades.

6) Calibration numbers: Speech Commands 10 raw at 0.5x frequency, S4 98.32 to 96.30 (dt-only); CKConv SC_raw 71.66 to 65.96 at 1/2 and 52.11 at 1/4 (seq[::n] subsampling); CKConv missing data (30/50/70% drop) 63.46/60.55/57.50. This angle has no HAR, EigenWorms or PDM numbers.

Access limits: the CROP paper body and the 2025 SFI journal paper were not read (403); MambaNO has no known arXiv id.

angle_summary:
Bottom line: most of what N2 would claim here is already in prior work or follows directly from it. Only a narrow FOH-specific and protocol-specific contribution appears to remain.

(1) The exact CDE solution already ignores the time grid of the same reconstructed path. This is the classical reparametrisation (tree-like) invariance. Kidger et al. (2020, App. B) say explicitly that series differing only by a collinear inserted point have the same interpolation, that they 'would often prefer' to treat them as equal, and that an observation-intensity channel tells them apart. Kidger's thesis (Sec. 3.5.2) says this invariance 'does not completely carry through to the numerical discretisation'. With s_j = j and a fixed unit step, an NCDE 'reduces to an RNN'. torchcde's recommended practice makes the solver grid depend on the knots, whether through jump_t at the knots for adaptive solvers or step_size set to the smallest gap. Hermite cubic interpolation with backward differences (torchcde's usual choice and Log-NCDE's NCDE baseline) changes when linear knots are inserted. N2's 'per-observation nonlinearity breaks invariance' counterexample is therefore a formalisation of a known remark, not a discovery.

(2) Exact input summaries with nonlinear updates only on a coarse grid are well established: the log-ODE family (NRDE, Log-NCDE, SLiCE), Logsig-RNN (2019, 2021) and Rough Transformers. Log-signatures of a piecewise-linear path over fixed physical-time windows are exactly invariant to collinear knot insertion. This follows from Chen's identity and reparametrisation invariance (primer, Corollary 1), but no paper states it as a knot-refinement theorem. Whether the published pipelines have this invariance depends on how windows are defined:
- NRDE uses t_i = i, and Log-NCDE's intervals are 'a fixed number of observations', so both break it.
- torchcde.logsig_windows uses physical-time windows with linearly interpolated boundaries. It therefore already implements 'exact PL summary plus a fixed physical-time nonlinear clock', but never states or tests the invariance.
- Rough Transformers use a 'fixed set of time points', but the code snaps boundaries to the last observation. Their Prop. 3.1 is only approximate (≈) and is tested with random drop.
- Logsig-RNN tests downsampling and missing data separately, and trains on sequences lengthened by linear interpolation.

(3) The biggest overlap is Walker et al. (2026, arXiv 2605.30213, Online Log-NCDEs). It builds exact interval log-signatures over physical-time query partitions that do not depend on observation times, and holds them fixed when inputs are dropped. Appendix A.5 states an exact invariance to inserting or removing 'value-preserving' observations, i.e. ZOH/rectilinear-type virtual knots. It also uses count coordinates to deliberately separate repeats from real measurements. That covers the refinement-invariance and knot-vs-measurement components of N2, for a ZOH-type reconstruction. The paper also argues against reconstructions based on interpolation.

(4) Other prior pieces that must be labelled as existing results:
- ZOH is the exact solution for piecewise-linear drivers, and Mamba is an Euler discretisation of a continuous gate integral (Cirone et al. 2024).
- Exact per-segment integration of a linear SSM over piecewise-linear paths, with a small-Δt-stable formulation (Exponentially Weighted Signature, 2026).
- Discretisation-bias bounds for NCDEs (Bleistein et al.).
- Grid independence only as the mesh goes to 0 for dt-rescaled controlled ResNets (neural signature kernels).

(5) What appears not covered in this angle:
- An exact first-order-hold (linear-interpolation) learnable diagonal linear-SSM stem feeding a standard fixed-step deep SSM on a physical clock, with a stated exact invariance theorem for FOH virtual knots.
- A controlled three-way protocol that separates lossless refinement, real downsampling with an explicit statement that aliasing is not recovered, and missing observations.
- Head-to-head tests against physical-window log-ODE (torchcde), RFormer and Online Log-NCDE baselines.
If N2's gains come mostly from a coarse fixed clock over exact summaries, the existing log-ODE, RFormer and Logsig-RNN models already explain them, which points to NO_GO under the user's criterion. Candidate distinctions are FOH versus ZOH invariance and SSM versus log-signature stems, and both must be shown empirically.

Calibration numbers:
- EigenWorms, 70/15/15 resplit with 23 duplicates removed: Log-NCDE 85.6±5.1 (depth 2, step 12); NRDE 83.9±7.3 (depth 2, step 4); NCDE 75.0±3.9; LRU 87.8±2.8; S5 81.1±3.7; S6 85.0±16.1; Mamba 70.9±15.8; BD-SLiCE 86±4; LNCDE with Log-ODE 88.3±3.7; LinOSS-IM 95.0±4.4.
- Rough Transformer 90.3±0.1 (10 windows); linear-interpolation resampling plus a vanilla Transformer 64.10%.
- NRDE's own paper: depth 2, step 4 gives 83.8±3.0.
- NCDE Speech Commands (MFCC, 161×20): 89.8±2.5%.
- None of these papers report HAR, PDM or a Speech Commands resolution change.

papers.title: TIDES: Implicit Time-Awareness in Selective State Space Models
papers.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv 2605.09742 (v1, 10 May 2026; paper marks itself as an anonymous submission)
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1 (incl. Our approach, Contributions); 2.1-2.3; 3.1; 3.2; 4 (Fading Flash, Findings); 5.1-5.3; 6; 7; App A (block order, timescale, GLU); App B.1 (ZOH); App C.1-C.4; App D.1-D.2; App F (random-drop details, Table 7); App G
papers.mechanism: A selective diagonal complex SSM (S5-style), with Re(Lambda_k), B_k and C_k computed from each input token u_k by affine or GLU heads with RMSNorm. Im(Lambda) stays static. The step size is the physical gap Delta_k = t_{k+1} - t_k and is not learned from the input. Each block is BN, then SSM, then GELU, then GLU, with dropout and a residual connection. Can be bidirectional. Mean pooling is not stated explicitly for classification.
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH: u_k is held constant on [t_k, t_{k+1}) and integrated exactly in closed form (App B.1). There is no FOH or linear-interpolant integration.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every observation token: the input-dependent Lambda_k, B_k and C_k per token, then GELU+GLU per token in every block, plus BatchNorm over batch and time.
papers.time_handling: Physical dt as the discretization step (Delta_tilde = Delta_k, set by timestamps), with a learnable per-mode timescale scaler. Mamba baselines instead receive Delta as an extra input channel.
papers.invariance_claim: No invariance claim for representations under a grid change. The claim is extrapolation to unseen Delta values 'by construction', because Delta enters only through the discretization, and this is shown empirically (Fading Flash, and EigenWorms with r_test different from r_train). Sec 2.1 states the semigroup property for the linear part. My analysis, not claimed by the paper: one TIDES SSM layer is exactly invariant to a knot inserted on the ZOH path with value u_k, because Lambda(u_k) and B(u_k) are unchanged and ZOH steps compose. The new output token and the per-token GELU/GLU, however, change the next layer's input sequence, and a knot on a linear interpolant changes even the first layer.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Fading Flash: a global Delta in {0.1,...,2.0}, trained on [0.5,1.5]. This rescales the whole trajectory; it is not refinement of the same path. EigenWorms random drop: a different random 50% of steps dropped at each training step, tested with fixed indices at r_test in {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9}, keeping the original timestamps. Physiome-ODE with 80% of values per channel randomly masked. UEA with no downsampling. No lossless knot refinement and no real-downsampling-with-aliasing test.

doubling $\Delta$ produces the same state evolution as integrating the continuous system for twice as long. (Sec 2.1)
Three projection heads compute the input-dependent SSM parameters from each input $u_{k}\in\mathbb{R}^{H}$ (Sec 3.2, Eq. 5)
Assuming the input $u(t)$ is held constant on $[t_{k},t_{k+1})$ at value $u_{k}$ , the exact solution of (8) is (App B.1, Eq. 10)
baking $\Delta$ in implicitly provides extrapolation across unseen timedeltas by construction. (Sec 4, Findings)

a different random 50% of timesteps is dropped at each training step; evaluation uses fixed indices at varying $r_{\mathrm{test}}$ , with original timestamps preserved to expose the elapsed gap. (Sec 5.3)
No data augmentation, time warping, or downsampling is applied. (App D.1, UEA protocol)
