Its design principle ('keep discretization and expressivity on separate ledgers') is conceptually adjacent to N2 but different: expressivity remains per observation. It does not separate knots from measurements, and downsampling is only random index drop, so aliasing is not studied. S5 at 0.419 on EigenWorms-drop with this tiny config is far below the full-data results; use with caution for calibration. There may be an inconsistency: Table 1 uses the Walker protocol but omits LinOSS.

papers.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling (S5)
papers.mechanism: A MIMO diagonalized continuous-time linear SSM with ZOH discretization and a learnable per-state timescale Delta, run with a parallel scan. Irregular sampling is handled by supplying a different A_bar_k (Delta_k) at each step. Layers are stacked with a GELU/sigmoid gate, then mean pooling.
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH of each sample over its step (Eq. 6). No interpolation.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every token: u'_k = GELU(y_k) * sigmoid(W GELU(y_k)) after each S5 layer. Norm, dropout and mean pooling are also computed over tokens.
papers.time_handling: dt as the step size. For irregular data, a per-step Delta_t comes from timestamps (pendulum). For a sampling-rate change, the learned Delta is rescaled globally by the rate ratio. Ablations: S5-drop (Delta_t set to 1) and S5-append (Delta_t appended as a channel).
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical and approximate: continuous-time parameterization allows applying the model at another sampling rate without retraining, by rescaling Delta. No exact invariance claim, and nothing on knot refinement.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Real downsampling: Speech Commands 16 kHz to 8 kHz by naive decimation, zero-shot. Irregular sampling: pendulum images (L=50 irregular samples from T=100). No lossless refinement and no random-drop sweep.
evidence_quotes: Parallel scans and the continuous-time parameterization also allow for efficient handling of irregularly sampled time series and other time-varying SSMs, by simply supplying a different $\overline{\mathbf{A}}_{k}$ matrix at each step. (Sec 3.3)

these models can be applied to datasets with different sampling rates without the need for re-training, simply by globally re-scaling the timescale parameter $\Delta$ by the ratio between the new and old sampling rates. (Sec 6.2)
Last column indicates 0-shot testing at 8kHz (constructed by naive decimation). (Table 2 caption)
the layer output of the activation function we apply is $\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\prime}=\mathrm{GELU}(\mathbf{y}_{k})\odot\sigma(\mathbf{W}*\mathrm{GELU}(\mathbf{y}_{k}))$ (App G.1)
S5-drop uses the same S5 architecture, but drops the dependence on the inter-sample interval, i.e. $\Delta_{t}\triangleq 1.0$ . (App F.3)
papers.reported_numbers: Speech Commands 35-way, 16 kHz / 8 kHz zero-shot (naive decimation): S5 96.52/94.53; S4-LegS 96.08/91.32; S4D-LegS 95.83/91.08; Liquid-S4 96.78/90.00; ConvNet 95.51/7.26; InceptionNet 61.24/5.18. Pendulum regression MSE x1e-3: S5 3.41 (0.27), S5-drop 6.68, S5-append 4.13, CRU (their rerun) 3.94, mTAND 65.64, ODE-RNN 7.26. (EigenWorms for S5 is reported elsewhere: 81.1+-3.7 under the Walker protocol.)
papers.notes: The canonical 'dt-only rescaling' baseline. Its sampling-rate test is real downsampling (decimation without an anti-alias filter, called 'naive'), so it mixes aliasing with the grid change. The irregular path uses ZOH of samples plus a per-token nonlinearity, so inserting virtual knots (e.g. linear-interpolated values) would change the input path under ZOH and add tokens. That is my inference; it is not tested.

papers.title: Multi-Time Attention Networks for Irregularly Sampled Time Series (mTAN)
papers.sections_read: 1; 3 (time embedding, multi-time attention, discretization); 4 (encoder-decoder, supervised); 5 (datasets, classification, Table 2); App A.1 (grep); A.3; A.4; code src/tan_classification.py (grep for reference points)
papers.mechanism: Learned time embeddings (linear + sinusoids) form query/key similarities. For each channel, a softmax-normalized kernel smoother of the observed values is computed at reference times. The resulting fixed-length sequence goes to a GRU (mTAND-Enc) or a VAE with an RNN encoder/decoder (mTAND-Full), then a classifier.
papers.input_reconstruction: None as an explicit path. It uses a learned attention kernel smoother (Nadaraya-Watson-like, normalized over the observed points) evaluated at reference points.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: The softmax attention weights depend nonlinearly on all observation times, and the normalization runs over observations. The GRU and MLP run on the fixed reference grid (128 points, linspace(0,1) in the code).
papers.time_handling: Continuous-time embedding of timestamps (normalized to [0,1]). The downstream network runs on a fixed reference grid.
papers.invariance_claim: None. Per my analysis, the softmax normalization over observations makes the interpolant depend on observation density, so inserting virtual knots changes it.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Naturally irregular data (PhysioNet, MIMIC-III), the 'Human Activity' dataset (UCI Localization Data for Person Activity), and synthetic interpolation with sparse observations. No controlled refinement or downsampling sweep.
evidence_quotes: the structure of the intermediate continuous-time function $\hat{x}_{hd}(t,\mathbf{s})$ is essentially a kernel smoother applied to the $d^{th}$ dimension of the time series. (Sec 3, Eq. 3)
The form of the attention mechanism is a softmax function over the observed time points $t_{id}$ for dimension $d$ . (Sec 3, Eq. 4)
the mTAN module can easily be adapted to produce such an output representation by materializing its output at a set of reference time points (Sec 3, Discretization)
For the classification tasks, we use $128$ reference points. (App A.4)
dim, torch.linspace(0, 1., 128), args.latent_dim, args.rec_hidden, 128, learn_emb=args.learn_emb (code src/tan_classification.py line 73)
papers.reported_numbers: Table 2: PhysioNet AUC mTAND-Enc 0.854+-0.001 and mTAND-Full 0.858+-0.004; MIMIC-III AUC 0.8419/0.8544; Human Activity (per-time-point accuracy, UCI Localization/Person Activity, not UCI-HAR smartphone) mTAND-Enc 0.907+-0.002, mTAND-Full 0.910+-0.002, ODE-RNN 0.885, GRU-D 0.862, IP-Nets 0.869. In ContiFormer's UEA random-drop Table 3, mTAN averages 0.7381/0.7118/0.6955 at 30/50/70% drop.
papers.notes: A 'fixed-clock network' precedent: the GRU runs on a fixed grid of reference times. It has no exact input integration and no invariance claim; its interpolant is density-weighted, and ContiFormer reports that its attention depends solely on time. It is the attention-style counterpart of the mandatory 'resample onto a fixed grid + backbone' baseline.

papers.title: Interpolation-Prediction Networks for Irregularly Sampled Time Series (IP-Nets)
papers.mechanism: A semi-parametric RBF interpolation network outputs, for each channel at evenly spaced reference times: a smooth interpolant, a transient component, and an intensity function (the sum of kernel weights). A cross-channel layer mixes them. A GRU prediction network runs on the regular reference grid. An auto-encoding loss is added.
papers.input_reconstruction: Normalized squared-exponential kernel smoothers (Nadaraya-Watson) at fixed reference points, plus an unnormalized intensity channel. This is not an exact interpolant.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: The GRU runs on the fixed, evenly spaced reference grid. The interpolation layer is a fixed-form kernel map with learned bandwidths and correlations.
papers.time_handling: Fixed evenly spaced reference time grid over a common interval (e.g. 48 h). Observation times enter only through the kernels.
papers.invariance_claim: None. By construction the intensity channel changes when points are added, and the normalized smoother changes when density changes (my analysis).
papers.grid_changes_tested: MIMIC-III (naturally irregular) and UWave, randomly subsampled to 10% of points.
evidence_quotes: The $T$ reference time points $r_{t}$ are chosen to be evenly spaced within that interval. (Sec 3.2)
the intensity functions $\bm{\lambda}_{d}$ to capture information about where observations occur in time. (Sec 3.2.1)
In this work, we conduct experiments leveraging a GRU network as the prediction network. (Sec 3.2.2)
we randomly sample 10% of the observations points from each time series to create a sparse and irregularly sampled data. (App A.1.2)
papers.reported_numbers: UWave 10% subsample and MIMIC-III numbers were not extracted. mTAN Table 2 reports IP-Nets at PhysioNet AUC 0.819, MIMIC-III 0.8390, and Human Activity (Localization) accuracy 0.869.
papers.notes: The oldest clear instance of 'nonlinear network on a fixed physical-time reference grid' fed by a learned resampler, with an explicit observation-intensity channel. It is close to the mandatory fixed-grid resampling baseline. The intensity channel deliberately encodes where observations occur, which is the opposite of treating virtual knots as non-information, though it gives a knot-versus-measurement handle.

papers.title: ContiFormer: Continuous-Time Transformer for Irregular Time Series Modeling
papers.sections_read: 3; 3.1 (continuous dynamics, query function, scaled dot product, expected values, CT-MHA); 3.2 (layer, sampling process); 4.2 (Table 3); C.2.1-C.2.2 (partial); D.3 (grep)
papers.mechanism: Each observation starts a key and a value trajectory evolved by a neural ODE. The query is a natural-cubic-spline interpolant of the per-observation queries. Attention logits are time-averaged integrals of q.k_i over [t_i, t], softmax over the N observations. FFN and LayerNorm follow, and the layer output is sampled at reference points before stacking.
papers.input_reconstruction: Natural cubic spline for queries and for the residual path. Keys and values are per-observation ODE trajectories, solved numerically with a fixed-step solver.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Softmax over all observations at each query time; the neural ODE vector fields inside the solver for each observation's key/value; FFN/LN at reference points, which are the input time points or task-specific times.
papers.time_handling: Continuous time via per-observation ODEs and integrals over [t_i, t]. Time is normalized to [0,1] (ablation D.6).
papers.invariance_claim: None about sampling. It claims continuous-time outputs ('almost' continuous without dropout) and gives an expressivity analysis. By my analysis, extra (virtual) observations add keys and values to the softmax, so the representation changes.
papers.grid_changes_tested: 20 UEA datasets with 30/50/70% of observations randomly dropped (NCDE protocol). EigenWorms is not included. Also irregular event sequences and a spiral interpolation task.
evidence_quotes: we define a closed-form continuous-time interpolation function (e.g., natural cubic spline) with knots at $t_{1},\ldots,t_{N}$ such that $\bm{\mathrm{q}}(t_{i})=Q_{i}$ (Sec 3.1, Query Function)
it utilizes ordinary differential equations to define the latent trajectories for each observation. (Sec 3.1)
These points are used to discretize the layer output, and can correspond to either the input time points (i.e., $\bm{\omega}$ ) or task-specific time points. (Sec 3.2, Sampling Process)
To generate irregular time series data, we follow the setting of  [30] to randomly drop either 30%, 50% or 70% observations. (Sec 4.2)
papers.code_url_and_license: No link in the arXiv HTML. It is commonly distributed in microsoft/SeqML, whose root LICENSE is MIT; the ContiFormer subfolder was not verified.
papers.notes: A task-appropriate 'resampling-free attention' baseline, too expensive for long signals (EigenWorms L=17,984). All three components rely on per-observation tokens.

papers.title: Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series with Missing Values (GRU-D)
papers.sections_read: 2; 2.1; 2.2 (Eqs 1-6 and GRU-D updates)
papers.mechanism: A GRU with trainable decays computed from the time since the last observation. Input decay moves a missing value from its last observation toward the empirical mean. Hidden-state decay is applied before each update. The mask is fed to the gates.
papers.input_reconstruction: None. Missing entries are imputed by a decayed forward-fill toward the mean (Eq. 5), and masks are kept.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every time step or observation (GRU gates, tanh, decay nonlinearity).
papers.time_handling: The time interval delta_t since the last observation feeds exp(-max(0, W delta + b)) decays. The time step is the sequence index.
papers.invariance_claim: None.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Naturally missing clinical data (PhysioNet, MIMIC-III). No controlled refinement or downsampling.
evidence_quotes: it is known that imputing the missing value with mean or forward imputation cannot distinguish whether missing values are imputed or truly observed. (Sec 2.1)

we use an input decay $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{\boldsymbol{x}}$ to decay it over time toward the empirical mean (which we take as a default configuration), instead of using the last observation as it is. (Sec 2.2)
This is implemented by decaying the previous hidden state $\boldsymbol{h}_{t-1}$ before computing the new hidden state $\boldsymbol{h}_{t}$ (Sec 2.2)
papers.reported_numbers: Not extracted from this paper. From other papers: CharacterTrajectories (NCDE Table 1) and UEA-drop averages in ContiFormer of 0.7284/0.7117/0.6725 at 30/50/70%; Latent ODE Human Activity (Localization) 0.806; mTAN Table 2 Human Activity 0.862; S7 Table 5 'HAR' (person activity) 83.57.

papers.notes: The standard missing-observation baseline. It explicitly separates observed values from imputed ones through masks, which is a prior version of the 'measured vs non-measured value' distinction. It has no continuous path and applies a per-observation nonlinear update.

papers.title: Latent ODEs for Irregularly-Sampled Time Series (ODE-RNN / Latent ODE)
papers.sections_read: 3.1 (Algorithm 1); 3.2 (partial); 3.3; 3.5; 4.5 (Tables 6-7)
papers.mechanism: ODE-RNN evolves the hidden state with a neural ODE between observations and applies an RNNCell jump at each observation. Latent ODE is a VAE with an ODE-RNN encoder and an ODE decoder from z0. An optional Poisson-process likelihood models the observation times.
papers.input_reconstruction: None. Observations enter as discrete RNN updates.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: The RNNCell at every observation, plus the neural ODE vector field evaluated continuously by the solver between observations.
papers.time_handling: Time dependence comes only implicitly through ODE integration over (t_{i-1}, t_i). There is no explicit dt input.
papers.invariance_claim: None.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Subsampled MuJoCo, PhysioNet (naturally irregular), and the Human Activity (Localization) per-time-point classification task.
evidence_quotes: We define the state between observations to be the solution to an ODE [...] and then at each observation, update the hidden state using a standard RNN update (Sec 3.1)
Our model does not explicitly depend on $t$ or $\Delta_{t}$ when updating the hidden state, but does depend on time implicitly through the resulting dynamical system. (Sec 3.1)
The fact that a measurement was made at a particular time is often informative about the state of the system (Che et al., 2018). (Sec 3.3)
The data consists of 3d positions of tags attached to their belt, chest and ankles (12 features in total). (Sec 4.5)

angle_summary:
1) No paper in this angle tests lossless knot refinement of the same reconstructed path. All reported grid changes fall into three kinds. (a) Random index drop: the 30/50/70% protocol from NCDE, reused by ContiFormer and RFormer; RFormer adds 85%; TIDES trains at 50% and tests r_test 0.1-0.9. (b) Naturally irregular data (PhysioNet, MIMIC, the Localization 'Human Activity' set, pendulum). (c) Real downsampling by naive decimation with Delta rescaling (S5 and Liquid-S4, Speech Commands 16 kHz to 8 kHz). None separates virtual knots from real measurements, apart from the conceptual remarks listed in point 3.

2) Nonlinear updates per observation or token are universal among the SSM and RNN baselines:
- per token: TIDES (input-dependent Re(Lambda), B, C plus GELU/GLU), S5 (GELU gate), S7, LinOSS (GLU), Liquid-S4 (sample products);
- per observation: GRU-D, ODE-RNN/Latent ODE, CRU (encoder, Kalman update, transition weights), Neural Flows;
- softmax over observations: ContiFormer, OsciFormer;
- softmax or normalized kernel over observations, which makes them density dependent: mTAN, IP-Nets.

TIDES and S5 integrate a ZOH-held input exactly with physical Delta. They claim Delta extrapolation or rescaling, not refinement invariance. My analysis, not claimed by the papers: a single ZOH-exact layer is invariant to a knot inserted on the ZOH path with the held value, but the per-token nonlinearity, pooling and depth break this, and a knot on a linear interpolant breaks even the first layer.

3) Closest prior art to the N2 central claim:
- **Rough Transformer (NeurIPS 2024): substantial overlap.** It computes exact signatures of the piecewise-linear interpolant over a fixed set of time windows and runs a Transformer only on those window tokens. Prop. 3.1 gives an approximate invariance, T(X) approximately equal to T(X'), under time reparameterization. The public code snaps window ends to the last observed index and uses one drop mask per run.
- **Neural CDE (NeurIPS 2020): substantial overlap.** Its representation depends only on the spline path. App. B states that ((0,0),(2,2)) and ((0,0),(1,1),(2,2)) give the same spline and 'we would often prefer that these time series be thought of as equal', and it uses an observational-intensity channel to distinguish them when needed.
- **IP-Nets and mTAN: partial overlap.** Both run a GRU on a fixed, evenly spaced reference grid, fed by a density-dependent kernel resampler; IP-Nets adds an explicit intensity channel.

So N2 cannot claim the principle ('the representation should depend only on the reconstructed path'), nor 'nonlinearity on a fixed time grid', as new. What N2 could still claim within this angle:
- a closed-form linear-SSM FOH stem, evaluated exactly at fixed physical clock times (interpolated endpoints, not snapped);
- a stated exact invariance to virtual knots, with numerical verification;
- an explicit three-way separation: refinement, then real downsampling with its aliasing limits (RFormer's workshop version already attributes a drop to aliasing below Nyquist), then missing data;
- a cost comparison.

Analytic caution for the NO_GO criterion: resampling the linear interpolant onto a fixed grid, then any backbone, is also exactly invariant to virtual knots on that interpolant. The mandatory resampling baseline therefore shares N2's refinement invariance. Any N2 advantage must come from integrating information between clock ticks (anti-aliasing and no point-sampling loss) or from behavior under real downsampling and missing data, not from refinement invariance itself.

angle: Exact discretization of linear SSMs for piecewise-linear inputs (first-order hold / triangle hold), phi-functions (exponential integrators, phi_1/phi_2 small-argument cancellation), and their use in deep SSMs (S4/S4D/S5/LRU/Mamba/Mamba-3, LS4, FlowState, irregular-time SSMs), plus canonical sources for (a) FOH exactness and semigroup/refinement invariance, (b) stable phi_2 evaluation, (c) Groenwall/variation-of-constants perturbation bounds, (d) h^2/8 linear-interpolation error, (e) aliasing under decimation. Adjacent 'exact functional of the piecewise-linear path + nonlinear processing on a window grid' models (NCDE/NRDE/Log-NCDE/Rough Transformer) were also checked because they share the same structure.
angle_summary:
What is STANDARD and must be cited, not claimed:
(a) FOH is exact for piecewise-linear inputs. Sources: Franklin-Powell-Workman, Digital Control of Dynamic Systems 3e, Sec. 6.3.2 'A Non-Causal First-Order-Hold Equivalent: The Triangle-Hold Equivalent'; MATLAB c2d('foh') docs ('exact match ... for piecewise linear inputs', also called 'ramp-invariant'); Hochbruck & Ostermann 2010, Acta Numerica, Sec. 2.2. In H&O Example 2.6 the s=2, c=(0,1) exponential quadrature is named the 'exponential trapezoidal rule', with weights phi_1-phi_2 and phi_2. That is exactly the FOH. H&O Theorem 2.7 / Corollary 2.8 bound the error by sum_j h_j^2 times the integral of ||f''||, which is zero for piecewise-linear f. The semigroup property is H&O eq. 2.4. Van Loan 1978 covers block-exponential evaluation. Refinement invariance for knots inserted on linear segments follows at once from exactness plus the flow property. No SSM paper states it as a theorem. Kidger et al. 2020 (NCDE, Remark B.13) do say that inserting a collinear point leaves the interpolant unchanged, and they deliberately treat the two series as equal. Caveat: ZOH is just as exactly invariant under refinements that keep its own staircase path. So any invariance must be stated relative to the reconstruction operator.
(b) phi-function cancellation for small arguments. Sources: Higham ASNA 2e, Sec. 1.14.1 'Computing (e^x-1)/x'; Kassam & Trefethen 2005, Sec. 2 (Table 2.1; Cox-Matthews use a Taylor cutoff; K&T use a contour integral); H&O Sec. 4.
(c) Perturbation bounds via variation of constants plus exponential stability. Canonical: Gronwall 1919, Bellman 1943, H&O Theorem 2.7. FlowState v3 (Jun 2026) Prop. B.3 already proves the two-rate ZOH mismatch bound ||B||M/alpha (1-e^{-alpha T}) max(Delta, Delta') and gives a multi-layer recursion. FSSM gives FOH-vs-ZOH cumulative error bounds.
(d) The h^2/8 |x''| bound for linear interpolation: de Boor, A Practical Guide to Splines, Ch. III eq. (2).
(e) Aliasing under decimation: Shannon/Nyquist; Oppenheim-Schafer DTSP Sec. 4.6.1 (section title verified only through search snippets). Deep-SSM precedents: S4ND Sec. 4.2 (aliasing when resolution changes; bandlimiting); SS-NO Theorem 4.1 (explicit aliasing term). S4 and S5 build their 8 kHz test sets by naive decimation, so 'dt-rescaling' results mix refinement effects with real downsampling.
FOH already used in deep SSMs:
- FSSM (ICASSP 2025) derives the exact FOH coefficients for selective Mamba with variable Delta_n (eq. 5). It then implements Taylor truncations, and its Delta is input-dependent.
- Beyond-ZOH (arXiv 2604.20606) benchmarks 'FOH' in Vision Mamba using a one-term formula.
- Mamba-3 (ICLR 2026) 'exponential-trapezoidal' is not exact FOH: its weights are lambda-weighted and Delta-scaled, with lambda data-dependent. The name collides with H&O's exact rule.
- S4 (bilinear) and S4D/S5/LRU/LS4/FlowState/TIDES/S2P2 (ZOH) all apply nonlinearities at every token.
Closest structural prior to N2's combination, which N2 must cite and set itself apart from:
- Rough Transformer (NeurIPS 2024): exact signatures of the piecewise-linear interpolant over 'a fixed set of time points', then a nonlinear Transformer on that fixed window grid. It claims only approximate invariance (Prop. 3.1). Its code snaps window boundaries to observation indices.
- NRDE / Log-NCDE: exact log-signatures over intervals r_i decoupled from the data, with the nonlinear vector field evaluated on the r_i grid. In practice r_i is set to a fixed number of observations.
If r_i were fixed in physical time, these models would already be exactly knot-refinement invariant.
Not found in this angle (possibly N2-specific; other angles should confirm):
1. An explicit exact-invariance theorem for a deep network whose nonlinearities read the stem only at clock times, including the FOH partial-interval query rule.
2. A minimal counterexample showing that per-observation nonlinearities break invariance even with exact per-layer ZOH/FOH, because a nonlinearity does not commute with interpolation. FlowState B.1 instead asserts that pointwise ops 'do not introduce additional temporal discretization error'. S2P2 B.4 only notes that inputs to deeper layers vary within intervals.
3. A protocol separating virtual knots, real downsampling and missing observations.
No HAR or PDM numbers were found in this angle.

||un - u(tn)|| <= C sum_{j=0}^{n-1} h_j^p int_{tj}^{tj+1} ||f^(p)(tau)|| dtau ... with a constant C that depends on T, but is independent of the chosen step size sequence. (Theorem 2.7)

papers.title: FlowState: Sampling-Rate-Equivariant Time-Series Forecasting
papers.sections_read: Abstract; Sec.3 (3.1 SSM encoder, 3.2 FBD, 3.3 Delta scaling); Sec.4 Sampling-Rate Equivariance; App. B.1 formal analysis (Assumptions B.1-B.2, Prop. B.3, pointwise ops, FBD, end-to-end bound, multi-layer remark); App. B.2 (part)
papers.mechanism: S5-style ZOH SSM encoder with an output gate and an MLP per layer, plus a functional-basis (Legendre) decoder. Encoder and decoder Deltas are scaled by factors s_Delta to match the sampling rate.
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH, stated explicitly: u_tilde(t)=u(floor(t/Delta)Delta).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every sample (output gate, residual, norm, MLP 'act independently at each time step').
papers.time_handling: dt rescaling: Delta_bar = s_Delta * Delta, with separate encoder and decoder factors.
papers.invariance_claim: APPROXIMATE equivariance. Single layer: ||s^(Delta)(T)-s^(Delta')(T)|| <= ||B||M/alpha (1-e^{-alpha T}) max(Delta, Delta') for Lipschitz input and exponentially stable A (Prop. B.3). End-to-end O(max Delta); multi-layer recursion E_l <= L_l E_{l-1} + C_l max(Delta, Delta').
papers.grid_changes_tested: Real rate changes: ETT1m vs ETT1h (subsampled) context, unseen sampling rates in GIFT-Eval. No lossless refinement test.
evidence_quotes: for a sampling interval Delta>0, the continuous input is replaced by the piecewise-constant reconstruction (App. B.1, eq. 19)
The discretized SSM is by definition exactly equivalent to the sampled solution of the continuous-time system driven by u^(Delta) (Åström and Wittenmark, 2013). (App. B.1)

These operations act independently at each time step and therefore do not introduce additional temporal discretization error. They may, however, amplify or attenuate the mismatch produced by the SSM state. (App. B.1, pointwise operations)
Therefore, FlowState is approximately sample-rate equivariant, with an approximation error vanishing as max{Delta,Delta'} -> 0. (Sec.4)
A full multi-layer proof requires tracking both the propagated mismatch from previous layers and the fresh ZOH discretization error introduced at each subsequent SSM layer. (App. B.1 remark)
papers.reported_numbers: Not recorded here (GIFT-Eval; qualitative ETT1m/ETT1h figures). No HAR/EigenWorms/SC.
papers.notes: This is the main 'dt-only rescaling' comparator, and it already contains the variation-of-constants perturbation bound (fact c). N2 must cite Prop. B.3 rather than re-derive it as new. Key contrast: FlowState's claim that pointwise ops add no temporal error is exactly what N2's counterexample disputes across layers, because a nonlinearity does not commute with interpolation and the next layer's ZOH reconstruction depends on the grid.

papers.title: HiPPO: Recurrent Memory with Optimal Polynomial Projections

papers.title: Stability and Discretization Error of State Space Model Neural Operators
papers.sections_read: Abstract; Sec.4 discrete framework; Theorem 4.1 + proof sketch; Sec.5.1 setup (subsampling experiments)
